**Objective:** Identify the parents of Patrick Flynn (born ~1845, Ireland; died 1908, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania).

| ID | Name | Gender | Key Facts |
|----|------|--------|-----------|

### Pedigree Analysis

**Minimum information — deficiencies:**
- Birth date is approximate (~1845); no month or day
- Birthplace is country-only (Ireland) — no county or parish
- Death is year-only; no day or month

**Gaps:**
- Both parents **completely unknown** — no parents recorded in FamilySearch
- No spouse or children recorded — FAN-club leads are absent and must be developed from records

- No occupational, military, or religious facts recorded

**FamilySearch entry is skeletal** — two bare facts, no sources attached, fully isolated in the tree.

**Historical context:** A birth of ~1845 places Patrick squarely in the Famine generation. Schuylkill County, PA is the anthracite coal belt — one of the largest destinations for post-Famine Irish emigrants. Naturalization records (First Papers, Second Papers) and death certificates from that county frequently name the Irish county of origin, which will be critical for crossing to Irish records.

**Known holdings:** None recorded.

### What's Missing (and Why It Matters)

| Gap | Why It Blocks Parent ID |
|-----|------------------------|
| Irish county/parish unknown | Can't search civil registration or parish registers without it |
| No spouse/children | FAN club is the standard path for Irish immigrant parent ID; must be built first |
| No naturalization record | First/Second Papers often name Irish county of origin |
| No death certificate | PA death certs (post-1906) name parents — this one may be in hand |

The death year of 1908 is significant: Pennsylvania began statewide death registration in 1906. A death certificate almost certainly exists and should name his parents directly — this is the highest-priority single record to locate.
